data.headline: Rio 2016: the first Olympic gold
data.standfirst: When rugby sevens joined the Olympics, Australia’s women won the first gold medal.

image.alt: Women’s teams in white and in blue contesting a lineout

body.text: Rugby returned to the Olympic Games at Rio 2016 in its sevens form, with men’s and women’s tournaments.
Australia’s women reached the final and beat New Zealand to become the first Olympic champions in rugby sevens.
Seven players a side and seven-minute halves make for a fast, open game, with tournaments played over a weekend. Speed and fitness count for as much as size.

data.headline: The Australia Sevens: the story so far
data.standfirst: Sevens is rugby at full speed: seven players a side and seven-minute halves, with tournaments played over a weekend.

image.alt: A team in red and white hoops gathered in front of the goal posts

body.text: Rugby sevens joined the Olympic Games at Rio 2016, where Australia’s women won the first gold medal, beating New Zealand in the final.
Both teams play a world series of tournaments every season, and the pathway runs from schools and clubs to state and national squads.
Players reach the Australia Sevens through club rugby, state teams and the national pathway. Every player who pulls on the jersey gets a cap number, counting every international since the first.

data.headline: A first-timer’s guide to a Test match
data.standfirst: Going to your first international? Here is how to make the most of the day.

image.alt: A floodlit stadium packed with spectators

body.text: A Test match is the biggest day on the rugby calendar. Crowds are bigger than at club or Super Rugby games, so a little planning goes a long way.
Public transport is usually the easiest way to reach the stadium. Gates open about two hours before kick-off, and arriving early means you see the warm-ups and are in your seat for the anthems.
Wear the colours and bring a jacket for night games. Kids are welcome, and many stadiums have family areas.
Expect queues for transport after the final whistle. Staying for a drink or a bite while the crowd clears often makes for an easier trip home.
